_strings.@@ab6ec6b14d82: Family Tax Credit (FTC) — Low-income WV resident individuals/families who file with at least one exemption. Enter the amount in the appropriate box for the credit being claimed. The schedule(s) must be submitted with tax return.'
_strings.@@bf3edade7d26: Homestead Excess Property Tax Credit (HEPTC) — Low-income owners of an owner-occupied WV residence whose WV real property tax paid (less any Senior Citizen Tax Credit) exceeds 4% of gross household income. Low-income means federal AGI of 300% or less of the federal poverty guideline for the household size. Homestead Exemption program participation is NOT required. No credit if any owner of the homestead is not a low-income person. Filers who pay federal AMT are flagged/excluded. Schedule HEPTC-1 and the Class 2 property tax receipt must be filed.

_strings.@@da799beef72c: Treaty conformity — WV conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from WV income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the WV return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: WV's resident return (Form IT-140) starts from federal adjusted gross income (line 1). The 2024 instructions state plainly (p.24): "The starting point for the West Virginia income tax return is your federal adjusted gross income." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from FAGI and flows through. WV's Schedule M "Modifications Increasing Federal Adjusted Gross Income" (lines 53-60) lists ONLY: interest/dividends on federal obligations exempt from federal but not state tax; interest/dividends on non-WV state/local bonds; interest on money borrowed to buy WV-exempt bonds; 402(e) lump-sum distributions; "Other income deducted from federal adjusted gross income but subject to state tax" (example given is IRC Section 199 income); and savings-plan/ABLE/Jumpstart withdrawals. There is NO add-back for tax-treaty income, foreign/nonresident-alien treaty income, or income excluded under a US tax treaty. Therefore treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by WV -> conforms = true.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form IT-140 line 8: 'Income Tax Due (Check One)' with method checkboxes 'Tax Table', 'Rate Schedule', 'Nonresident/Part-year resident calculation schedule'. Line 7 feeding it reads 'West Virginia Taxable Income (line 4 minus lines 5 & 6) IF LESS THAN ZERO, ENTER ZERO'. Instructions p.24: 'LINE 8 WEST VIRGINIA INCOME TAX - Check the appropriate box to indicate the method you used to calculate your tax.' Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): surviving_spouse ($2,000 — Exemptions box (d): 'A surviving spouse may claim an additional exemption for the two (2) taxable years following the year in which the spouse died, provided he/she has not remarried before the end of the taxable year' (instructions p.24). One more $2,000 exemption included in box (e). NOT applied by calc.state_tax (the engine applies only the personal/dependent keys) — claim it on the form, or reflect it by raising exemptions_count only if eligible.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: TY2024 verification (2026-08-01): the 2024 booklet prints the SAME rate schedules and constants as TY2023 — the further across-the-board reduction (W. Va. Code §11-21-4i) applies beginning TY2025, not TY2024. Constants re-derived: 236.00/708.50/1,239.50/2,183.50 equal exact cumulative marginal sums; Schedule II constants are exactly half-boundary equivalents. Base guidance: Supply Form IT-140 line 4, West Virginia Adjusted Gross Income = line 1 federal adjusted gross income ('Enter your federal adjusted gross income as shown on Federal Form 1040') plus line 2 additions to income (Schedule M line 61) minus line 3 subtractions from income (Schedule M line 52). If the filer has no Schedule M modifications, line 4 equals federal AGI. The op then subtracts the shipped $2,000-per-exemption amounts (standard_deduction is 0 — West Virginia has none) to reproduce line 7 West Virginia Taxable Income, assuming line 5 (Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion, only available when federal AGI is $10,000 or less / $5,000 MFS) is zero. Adjudication note (two-pass): standard_deduction is null — West Virginia allows neither a standard deduction nor itemized deductions on Form IT-140 (the only base reductions are the $2,000-per-exemption line 6 amounts, shipped as personal/dependent). Rate-schedule constants re-verified against the 2024 IT-140 booklet (236.00 / 708.50 / 1,239.50 / 2,183.50). THE 2023 RATES CONTINUE (corrected 2026-09-28, Phase J JS2 — this note had misdated the statute): the shipped rates (2.36%/3.15%/3.54%/4.72%/5.12%) are the schedule printed in the official 2024 IT-140 booklet (p.35), and they are the 2023 rates unchanged. They were enacted by 2023 HB 2526, codified at W. Va. Code §11-21-4g, which states the rates 'shall apply retroactively for all taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2023, and shall be in lieu of the rates of tax specified in §11-21-4e of this code' (https://code.wvlegislature.gov/11-21-4G/, fetched 2026-09-28). There was no 2024 rate cut; do not use a pre-2023 rate table. TWO RATE SCHEDULES: Rate Schedule I applies 'if you checked 1 (Single), 2 (Head of household), 3 (Married filing joint), or 5 (Widow[er] with dependent child)'; it is duplicated here for single, married_filing_jointly, and head_of_household. Rate Schedule II applies only to filing status 4 (Married filing separately); its bracket bounds ($5,000/$12,500/$20,000/$30,000) were copied directly from the published schedule, not derived. The printed constants ($236.00/$708.50/$1,239.50/$2,183.50 on Schedule I; $118.00/$354.25/$619.75/$1,091.75 on Schedule II) exactly equal the cumulative sums of the prior brackets — no rounding divergence. TAX TABLE MANDATE BELOW $100,000: Line 8 instructions (p.24) — 'If your filing status is single, head of household, widow(er) with a dependent child or married filing jointly and your taxable income is less than $100,000, apply the amount of taxable income shown on line 7 to the Tax Table on page 36 and enter your tax on this line'; the rate schedule is for taxable income over $100,000. The table (booklet pp.36–40, last row $99,950–100,000 = $4,230) is band-midpoint based, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands — the filed form must use the table. Married-filing-separately filers CANNOT use the table at any income: 'If your filing status is Married Filling Separately you MUST use RATE SCHEDULE II to compute your tax.' NO STANDARD OR ITEMIZED DEDUCTION: West Virginia allows neither a standard deduction nor federal itemized deductions on Form IT-140 — the only across-the-board deduction is the $2,000-per-exemption allowance ('You can deduct $2,000 for every exemption claimed in your exemption schedule', p.24). standard_deduction is shipped as 0 for every filing status so the engine subtracts exemptions only. ZERO-EXEMPTION $500 ALLOWANCE NOT MODELED: 'If you claimed zero exemptions, enter $500 on this line [line 6]' (box (e) = 0, e.g. a filer claimable as a dependent on another return). The engine with exemptions_count=0 subtracts $0, not $500, so it can overstate tax by up to about $26 (5.12% of $500) for such filers — use the form's line 6 in that case. LOW-INCOME EARNED INCOME EXCLUSION (LINE 5) NOT MODELED: filers with federal AGI of $10,000 or less ($5,000 or less MFS) who have earned income may exclude the smaller of federal AGI, earned income, or $10,000 ($5,000 MFS) on line 5 before line 7 (worksheet, booklet p.29). The engine assumes line 5 = 0; it only affects returns with federal AGI at or below $10,000/$5,000. SCHEDULE M MODIFICATIONS COME BEFORE THE SUPPLIED BASE: the senior-citizen modification (up to $8,000 of income per taxpayer age 65+ or permanently/totally disabled), the up-to-$8,000 surviving-spouse decreasing modification, Social Security benefit modification, and all other Schedule M items are line 2/line 3 adjustments taken BEFORE line 4 — the caller must supply line 4 WV AGI already reflecting them. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE: the engine maps QSS to married_filing_jointly. West Virginia's own filing status 5, 'Widow(er) with dependent child', uses the SAME Rate Schedule I as married filing jointly and the same $2,000 exemptions, so the mapping reproduces the correct tax. ROUNDING: the booklet requires whole dollars ('Round off amounts to WHOLE DOLLARS – NO CENTS', p.14) and both rate-schedule examples say 'Round to nearest whole dollar' — consistent with the engine's half-up rounding to whole dollars. LINE 7 FLOOR: 'IF LESS THAN ZERO, ENTER ZERO' matches the engine's max(0, base_after). CREDITS ARE NOT EXEMPTIONS AND ARE NOT MODELED: line 8 tax is reduced on line 9 by the Tax Credit Recap Schedule credits — notably the Family Tax Credit (Schedule FTC-1), which can reduce the line 8 tax by up to 100% for low-income families based on family size and Modified Federal AGI, plus the refundable Senior Citizen Tax Credit (line 18) and Homestead Excess Property Tax Credit (line 19), the Build WV refundable credit (line 20) and the three WV Property Tax Adjustment Tax Credits (line 21 boxes A/B/C). The engine computes line 8 only; actual line 10 liability may be lower. No county or municipal income tax is collected through Form IT-140 — the return computes only the West Virginia state personal income tax.
